instruction: I'm trying to use 'pip' but getting "command not found". Could you help me set up pip3 as the default pip by creating an appropriate alias in my shell configuration?

command: import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'alt', 't'); time.sleep(0.5)

metadata.explanation: Task requires adding pip=pip3 alias to .bashrc to fix 'pip: command not found'. Evaluator checks if the alias exists in .bashrc. Same complexity as original - fixing command not found via shell configuration.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator now checks 4 common shell config files (.bashrc, .bash_profile, .zshrc, .profile) covering most use cases - addresses previous concern about only checking .bashrc

Uses flexible regex pattern '^[[:space:]]*alias[[:space:]]+pip[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*['\"]?pip3['\"]?' that accepts various valid alias formats including different quoting styles (single quotes, double quotes, no quotes) and optional spacing - addresses previous strict matching concern
Expected value '1\n' correctly includes newline character matching shell command output format
Getter logic correctly returns 1 if alias found in any of the checked config files, 0 otherwise - proper OR logic with grep commands
Metric 'exact_match' appropriately compares binary result (1 vs 0) with expected value
Evaluator can semantically verify that the instruction requirement (creating alias in shell configuration) has been completed
Minor limitation: doesn't check less common config files like .zprofile or .bash_aliases, but these are edge cases and the 4 checked files cover the vast majority of shell configurations
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Optional enhancement: Could add .zprofile for additional zsh coverage and .bash_aliases for Debian-based systems, though this is a minor edge case improvement
